subject: Aligning Dedicated-demo: ops checklist + QPS/latency expectations
messages:
From: Alex Grover <alex@cloudline.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: sanjay@cloudline.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Cloudline: Requesting Dedicated capacity demo (throughput + latency)

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick self-serve signup — we kicked the tires on the hosted API and are interested in a deeper session on Dedicated so we can estimate latency and per-token cost at our peak QPS.

High level: we're a streaming analytics vendor. We need a demo that covers:
- baseline p50/p95 token latency with batch sizes 1-8
- expected tokens/sec per reserved GPU profile
- warmup/cold-start behavior and KV cache warmup

Are you able to run a 45-minute walkthrough next week? We can share an approximate QPS profile and a sample prompt set. Attaching a brief CSV with our expected peak QPS and sequence lengths.

Thanks,
Alex

--
Alex Grover
Head of Infrastructure, Cloudline Labs
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Alex Grover <alex@cloudline.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cloudline: Requesting Dedicated capacity demo (throughput + latency)

Alex — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the CSV — that helps a lot.

Suggested plan:
1) 15m intro: Cloudline goals + critical SLAs (what latency matters at what percentile)
2) 20-25m technical walkthrough: how Redwood Dedicated maps QPS->reserved slots, autoscale behavior, and live throughput run on a representative model/seq len
3) 5-10m next steps / procurement requirements (pricing bands, contract timelines)

We can do Tue/Wed next week morning PT. Ben will run the throughput demo and Priyom will cover pricing/ops. I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm a slot.

Attaching: network-topology.pdf and a quick demo agenda.

Best,
Irene

Irene Choi
Enterprise SDR Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Grover <alex@cloudline.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: sanjay@cloudline.ai
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cloudline: Requesting Dedicated capacity demo (throughput + latency)

Hi Irene — thanks, that agenda looks perfect. Quick notes before we lock time:
- The CSV lists peaks in UTC; converting to PT, our likely preferred window is 8–11am PT Tue/Wed.
- One ask: can you include a short section on multi-tenant fallback behavior? If Dedicated hits a temporary cap, what's the behavior and what's the auto-fallback to hosted like?
- Also curious about QPS shaping recommendations for us (we have bursty traffic).

We can do Tue May 18th 9:30am PT — does that work?

Alex
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Alex Grover <alex@cloudline.ai>, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cloudline: Requesting Dedicated capacity demo (throughput + latency)

Thanks Alex — 9:30am PT Tue May 18 works on our side. Quick operational notes up front:
- For the live throughput run we'll provision a temporary reserved pool matching the CSV's peak QPS; this is a staging reservation and won't affect your billing beyond the agreed demo credit.
- Fallback behavior: Redwood can route requests to a verified compatible model in the hosted pool with a configurable policy (latency-first, cost-first, or strict deny). We'll demo both the hard-fail and graceful-fallback behaviors.
- For bursty workloads we recommend a small buffer of reserved capacity + autoscale windowing; we'll show a couple configs and expected token/sec curves.

I'll open a collaborative Google Doc for run notes and ask you to paste a short representative prompt set. Priyom will bring the pricing bands and contract timeline at the end.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Grover <alex@cloudline.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: sanjay@cloudline.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cloudline: Requesting Dedicated capacity demo (throughput + latency)

Perfect — confirmed for Tue May 18, 9:30am PT. I've uploaded the final prompt set and an updated CSV to the drive link below. One more ask: during the demo can you show p95 with both batch=1 and batch=4? We want to understand latency tradeoffs in our streaming path.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cCloudlineDemo

See you all then — Alex

Attachments referenced: throughput_requirements.csv, redwood-demo-agenda.pdf
